title: The Boy Who Hits Sixes for Breakfast: Sooryavanshi Rewrites IPL History at 15
excerpt: Rajasthan Royals' teenage phenom surpasses Abhishek Sharma's single-season mark, earning India A honours and global admiration along the way
body:
When Vaibhav Sooryavanshi walked out to open the batting against Delhi Capitals at the Arun Jaitley Stadium on May 17, nobody in the ground doubted what was coming. The first ball from Lungi Ngidi sailed into the stands — a statement of intent from a 15-year-old who has turned IPL 2026 into his personal batting laboratory. By the time he was dismissed for 46 off 21 balls, Sooryavanshi had done what no Indian batter had ever done before: hit 43 sixes in a single IPL season.

## The Record Falls

The previous mark belonged to Abhishek Sharma, who smashed 42 sixes during Sunrisers Hyderabad's exhilarating 2024 campaign. That Sooryavanshi surpassed it while still a year away from being eligible to vote speaks volumes about the generational shift in Indian cricket. His three sixes against DC — clean, authoritative strikes against international-class pace bowling — took him past the milestone with the casual certainty of a batsman who does not appear to understand the concept of nervous nineties, metaphorical or otherwise.

## A Season for the Ages

The numbers from Sooryavanshi's debut IPL campaign read more like a video game save file than a real cricket scorecard. In 18 matches for Rajasthan Royals, he has accumulated 692 runs at a strike rate of 224.67 — a figure that would be impressive for a seasoned T20 mercenary, let alone a schoolboy. He has two centuries, including a blistering 103 off just 37 balls against Sunrisers Hyderabad that became the fastest hundred by an Indian teenager in IPL history. For context, after the same number of opening innings in this season, Virat Kohli — the most prolific run-scorer in IPL history — has 565 runs at a strike rate of 128.99. Sooryavanshi has outscored him by 127 runs and nearly doubled his six count.

The praise from his peers has been unstinting. **Kagiso Rabada**, one of the finest fast bowlers of his generation, summed it up with characteristic directness: "There's not an ounce of fear in his body." Ravi Shastri, India's former head coach, went further, publicly calling for Sooryavanshi's immediate inclusion in India's T20I squad for the upcoming series against Ireland. "I don't care if he's 14 or 16," Shastri told broadcasters. "He's ready."

## A Target Still in Sight

The all-time record for sixes in a single IPL season remains Chris Gayle's 59, set during the Jamaican's legendary 2012 campaign for Royal Challengers Bangalore. With Rajasthan Royals still alive in the playoff race and potentially two matches remaining, Sooryavanshi has an outside shot at the record — he needs 17 sixes from a possible two innings, a tall order but one that nobody would rule out given the trajectory of his season.

## The Diaspora Watches

For the millions of Indian cricket fans scattered across the globe — in London pubs at odd hours, in Bay Area living rooms with JioHotstar on the big screen, in Toronto basements where WhatsApp groups light up with every boundary — Sooryavanshi has become the most compelling reason to set the alarm. His emergence has sparked a particular fervour among younger NRI fans, many of whom see in him a generational peer rather than a distant legend. In an era when Indian cricket's brightest stars are in their mid-thirties, a 15-year-old who plays with the abandon of a street cricketer but the technique of a coached professional has become a symbol of renewal.

## What Comes Next

The BCCI has already shown its hand. Sooryavanshi has been named in India A's squad for the upcoming tri-series against Sri Lanka A and Afghanistan A, with matches in Galle and Dambulla starting June 9. A strong showing there, combined with his IPL exploits, could fast-track him into the senior squad for the T20I series against Ireland later in the summer. At 15, he has time — perhaps the most valuable commodity in sport. The question is whether Indian cricket has the patience to let him accumulate it, or whether the weight of expectation will demand acceleration.
